| [THEORY-111](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-111.md) v2 | Along a low-loss linear path between two networks, every layer's features are the interpolation of the endpoints' features, so averaging weights within a basin averages features | Zhou et al. (2023), [LIT-674](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-674.md): whenever two image classifiers are linearly mode connected, by spawning or by permutation, the features of nearly every layer of the interpolated network are proportional to the interpolation of the endpoints' features. This is layerwise linear feature connectivity, and two conditions, weak additivity of ReLU and a commutativity of weights with features, imply it exactly. Lubana et al.'s Lemma 2, [LIT-669](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-669.md), gives the exact one-hidden-layer case: linear connectivity between interpolating minima forces shared activation patterns, and with shared patterns the hidden features are linear along the path. Measured on pairs at three interpolation points, image classification only. The step to many-model averages such as soups and SWA is not measured. | Proposed |

Permute-then-average fails, which they explain by the permuted model lying in a basin for its own task only. Mean cross-model feature correlation falls with depth (0.50, 0.37, 0.27 at three depths). Merging only the early layers and keeping later layers as task heads recovers most of the ensemble's accuracy. Merging features within one model as well as across both helps once the models are wide enough to hold redundant features. With full merging on ImageNet-1k, ZipIt! is no better than permutation (8.6%). No same-task control separates the effect of task difference from that of depth. | Proposed |

(2022), [LIT-858](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-858.md), in a toy built for it: same-answer training pairs force equal embedding sums, equal sums carry answers to unseen pairs, and for addition with p = 10 the fraction at which the forced equations first pin the embedding to a + kb (about 0.4) matches the onset of generalisation and Power et al.'s critical fraction ([LIT-341](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-341.md)). It is shown for one size, 1D embeddings and an operation built into the architecture. It is not shown that larger networks generalise by this mechanism, and for S₃ the networks generalise beyond it. | Active |
| [THEORY-182](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-182.md) v2 | A rank-limited contrastive word embedding trained from small initialisation learns the top eigenvectors of the co-occurrence matrix's relative deviation from independence, one at a time in order of eigenvalue, not the best low-rank approximation of its unconstrained optimum | Karkada, Simon, Bahri and DeWeese (2025), [LIT-855](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-855.md): for the quartic approximation of word2vec with tied weights and symmetric, constant-weight reweighting, the minimisers are proved and the stepwise order is derived, and the prediction matches trained word2vec far better than truncated PMI. It is shown for a proxy of word2vec, not for word2vec, and the dynamics are an approximate derivation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-183](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-183.md) v2 | When the co-occurrence of words on a latent continuum depends only on their separation, a spectral word embedding places them on the Fourier modes of that continuum, so the circles and rippled curves of months, years and places come from a symmetry of the corpus statistics | Karkada, Korchinski, Nava, Wyart and Bahri (2026), [LIT-860](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-860.md): proved for an embedding whose Gram matrix equals the co-occurrence matrix (or its absolute value) at full rank, with the exponential kernel solved for both boundary conditions; the symmetry measured in Wikipedia; matching PCA pictures in Gemma 2. That trained networks get their geometry this way is inferred, not tested: nothing in the paper changes the statistics and watches the geometry follow. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-185](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-185.md) v4 | When each binary attribute of a word affects its co-occurrence independently and multiplicatively, the PMI is affine in the attributes with rank at most d + 1, so a spectral PMI embedding is a linear image of the attribute hypercube and parallelogram analogies hold exactly; over the full hypercube of words, each attribute's two values equally frequent, the raw co-occurrence ratio mixes in products of attributes, and keeps exact analogies only when the strengths are alike enough that every attribute mode outranks every product mode | Korchinski, Karkada, Bahri and Wyart (2025), [LIT-863](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-863.md): proved for a generative model of co-occurrence in which words are bundles of independent binary attributes, with robustness to noise, pruning and deleted pairs argued from eigenvalue bounds and simulated. The embeddings are eigendecompositions, not trained models; that real co-occurrence is close to this form is inferred from spectral and accuracy-curve shapes, not measured. | Active |
| [THEORY-186](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-186.md) v3 | A deep linear network trained from small weights learns the singular modes of its input–output correlations one at a time in order of strength, each in a sharp sigmoidal transition, while a shallow network learns them all together; the stages come from the product of layers and the data's spectrum, not from nonlinearity | Saxe, McClelland and Ganguli (2019), [LIT-862](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-862.md), restating their 2014 solution (LIT-864): exact for decoupled, balanced initial weights and white inputs, simulated for random small weights. With hierarchically generated data the spectrum falls with depth in the tree, so the schedule is coarse to fine. It is not a claim about nonlinear networks, about correlated inputs, or about learning that starts from prior knowledge. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-189](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-189.md) v2 | Nested angular cones in the Poincaré ball, symmetric about the outward ray with an aperture depending only on the apex's radius, are transitive only if the aperture is at most π/2 and r sin ψ(r)/(1 − r²) does not increase outward; so no such cone can be defined near the origin, the widest admissible family is sin ψ = K(1 − r²)/r, and every point a cone contains lies farther from the origin than its apex | Ganea, Bécigneul and Hofmann (2018), [LIT-866](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-866.md): Lemma 2 and Theorem 3 prove the necessity half under four stated requirements on the cones; the transitivity of the closed-form family (Theorem 4), which the source asserts without proof, is proved in this record's note of 2026-10-19; the radial monotonicity is this record's derivation from the hyperbolic law of cosines. It says what a cone order on the ball can be, not which posets embed in it, and nothing about meets, joins or learned embeddings. | Active |
| [THEORY-194](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-194.md) v5 | On Monte Carlo samples of the 2D Ising model and of the 2D dimer model with added noise spins, a block coarse-graining trained to maximize mutual information with the system beyond a buffer recovered the variables renormalization already uses (Kadanoff block spins; the dimers' low-momentum electric fields, with no weight on the noise), and iterated on 128 × 128 Ising samples gave the flow away from the critical point, locating it to about 1% and giving ν ≈ 1.0 ± 0.15, while a restricted Boltzmann machine trained by contrastive divergence on the noisy dimer data coupled to the noise and to columnar patterns instead | Koch-Janusz and Ringel (2017), [LIT-873](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-873.md): shown numerically on two 2D lattice models whose relevant variables were known (Ising block spins, dimer electric fields), with an iterated Ising flow giving T_c to about 1% and ν ≈ 1.0 ± 0.15, and analytically only for 1D and quasi-1D chains. The general equivalence of the objective with a short-ranged effective Hamiltonian is argued, not proved, and no system with unknown relevant variables was tried. | Active |
| [THEORY-195](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-195.md) v3 | On the Random Hierarchy Model, in the experiments reported (s = 2, L ≤ 4, small v), deep CNNs matched to the tree and trained in a feature-learning regime reach a tenth of chance error from about n_c m^L examples, polynomial in the input dimension, at the training-set size at which their hidden layers become invariant to swapping synonymous tuples; two-layer networks and the same CNNs as fixed kernels need a number proportional to the whole input space, exponential in the input dimension, and deep CNNs stay near chance when every tuple is made equally likely in every class | Cagnetta, Petrini, Tomasini, Favero and Wyart (2023), [LIT-877](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-877.md): measured for depth-(L + 1) CNNs and deep fully connected networks on the Random Hierarchy Model with s = 2 and L ≤ 4, with a large-v scaling argument for the correlation threshold and an exact one-step-gradient model of a two-layer network on one patch. The law n_c m^L is fitted, not proved for trained deep networks, and in this model the correlation threshold and the grammar's size are the same expression, so the data cannot say which of the two sets it. | Active |
| [THEORY-196](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-196.md) v2 | A finite tree embeds in the hyperbolic plane with worst-case distortion 1 + ε, but because a hyperbolic distance d takes about d bits to write, its coordinates need Θ((ℓ/ε) log deg_max) bits: logarithmic in the branching, linear in the longest path ℓ, so hyperbolic space is economical for shallow bushy hierarchies and not for deep ones | Sala, De Sa, Gu and Ré (2018), [LIT-874](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-874.md). The upper bound is Sarkar's construction with the paper's bit count. The lower bound is proved for H² and one family of trees, with an approximation, and dimension's help is shown only as an upper bound. The cost is a cost of coordinates in a fixed-point model, not of the information in the tree, and it says nothing about Euclidean or linear-direction representations of the same hierarchy. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-197](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-197.md) v4 | Mehta and Schwab's correspondence between Kadanoff's variational renormalization group and restricted Boltzmann machines is an identity of parametrizations, under which an exact RG step is a perfect fit of the data distribution; away from that point it does not make training by distribution fitting a renormalization | Mehta and Schwab (2014), [LIT-882](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-882.md), Eqs. 18–22: setting the RG kernel T = −E + H makes the RG coarse Hamiltonian equal the RBM's hidden-marginal Hamiltonian for every parameter value, and Kadanoff's exactness condition equal to zero KL divergence. Short of exactness the paper itself says the two use different variational schemes, and Koch-Janusz and Ringel ([LIT-873](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-873.md)) give a case where distribution fitting keeps the wrong variables. The free-energy part of the argument was derived independently here; Lin, Tegmark and Rolnick's v2 appendix makes it in substance (LIT-887). | Active |
| [THEORY-200](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-200.md) | On sparse hierarchical data, deep networks become insensitive to swapping synonymous parts and to small displacements of informative features at the training-set size at which they learn the task | Tomasini and Wyart (2024), [LIT-880](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-880.md): measured for locally connected, convolutional and fully connected networks on the Sparse Random Hierarchy Model with s ≤ 3 and L ≤ 3, with thresholds for the two sensitivities tuned per setting; the sample size is about (s0 + 1)^L n_c m^L times s^(L/2) without weight sharing, with a one-step argument for the (s0 + 1)^L, and about (s0 + 1)^2 n_c m^L with it, unexplained. Both invariances keep the parent's label statistics by construction, so the model shows that trained networks do the grouping, not that the invariances could not separate, and the extension to images is an analogy. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-201](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-201.md) v2 | In next-token prediction on hierarchically generated sequences, the correlation between two tokens falls by about a factor m per level of their common ancestor, so a training set of P sequences resolves correlations only out to a distance t*(P) at which they meet sampling noise; learners come to represent the hidden symbols up to that depth, giving loss steps at about v m^(2ℓ−1) examples, and on character-level text the context at which the loss saturates grows as P^(1/(2β)) with β the measured correlation decay | Cagnetta and Wyart (2024), [LIT-883](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-883.md), extending [LIT-877](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-877.md) from labels to masked tokens: the correlation plateaus and the noise floor are derived for the Random Hierarchy Model in the large-v, large-m limit; the loss steps and the representation probes are measured in small transformers and CNNs; the link between them is argued, not proved; and the real-text evidence, from two character-level corpora, tests the effective context window, not the hierarchy. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-202](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-202.md) v3 | In variational renormalization over general Boltzmann machines, neither a matched partition function nor Kadanoff's exact trace condition makes a coarse-graining a renormalization: the first holds for joint Hamiltonians whose marginal is not the data, the second for hidden variables that do not interact with the system, so the variables a renormalization keeps must be fixed by a further stated condition | Lin and Tegmark (2016), [LIT-887](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-887.md), arXiv v1–v2 appendix, a part dropped from the journal text: a family of joint Hamiltonians with Z_tot = Z and the wrong marginal, and the remark that any non-interacting pair meets the trace condition. Under Mehta and Schwab's identification ([LIT-882](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-882.md)) the trace condition is a perfect fit of the data, so even an exact variational RG step leaves the coarse variables' meaning free. The restricted Boltzmann machine proper needs visible–visible terms for the second construction; that narrows the example, not the claim. Promoted on 2026-10-20 with both constructions re-derived. Whether the trace condition suffices inside Kadanoff's kernel families is QUESTION-205. | Active |
| [THEORY-212](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-212.md) | In a two-layer linear network trained by gradient flow, the relative scale of the two layers, which gradient flow conserves, sets the learning regime: balanced layers learn in sigmoidal stages and both build task-specific representations, while strongly unbalanced layers learn exponentially with a static kernel and leave the larger layer task-agnostic | Dominé et al. (2025), [LIT-943](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-943.md), read in [NOTE-715](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-715.md). With whitened inputs and a λ-balanced start, W₂ᵀW₂ − W₁W₁ᵀ = λI, the full gradient flow is solved exactly. λ is conserved and sets the regime. As λ → 0, singular values are learned in sigmoidal stages, as in Saxe et al., and both layers become task-specific. As \|λ\| → ∞, learning is exponential, the NTK is static, and the larger layer stays near the identity while the smaller carries the task at scale ∝ 1/\|λ\|. The paper analyses gradient flow only. Under SGD the conserved quantity drifts ([THEORY-211](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-211.md)), which [QUESTION-081](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-081.md) takes up. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-227](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-227.md) | Mutual information between an input and its representation does not fix the representation's quality: invertible encoders all preserve it exactly, yet under a linear probe some do better than the raw input and some worse | Tschannen, Djolonga, Rubenstein, Gelly & Lucic (2020), [LIT-247](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-247.md), read in [NOTE-749](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-749.md). Invertible RealNVP encoders on MNIST halves keep the true MI constant, yet trained with an MI estimator they gain linear-probe accuracy, and one trained adversarially against a linear probe ends "significantly worse than using raw pixels". At matched bound values the encoder architecture decides quality. What makes MI-trained representations good must therefore come from somewhere other than MI. The paper's alternative, that InfoNCE works as metric learning, is argued, not tested. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-228](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-228.md) v2 | On a finite augmentation space, at the population optimum of the spectral contrastive loss with k ≥ 2r, linear-probe error is bounded, up to constant and logarithmic factors, by the error of recovering the label from an augmentation divided by the squared sparsest-partition conductance of the augmentation graph | HaoChen, Wei, Gaidon & Ma (2021), [LIT-249](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-249.md), read in [NOTE-740](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-740.md). On a finite augmentation space, with labels recoverable from augmentations up to error α and k ≥ 2r, every population minimizer of the spectral contrastive loss has linear-probe error Õ(α/ρ²_⌊k/2⌋), where ρ is the sparsest-partition conductance of the augmentation graph (Thm 3.8). The guarantee needs no conditional independence of the views given the label. It is a statement about the population optimum of one loss: it says nothing about what training reaches, nothing about InfoNCE, and its infinite-space extension is asserted, not proved. | Active |
| [THEORY-229](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-229.md) v3 | For a symmetrized Barlow Twins loss on a linear or fixed-kernel model, gradient flow from a small initialization of common scale aligned with the top eigenvectors of the pairs' symmetrized cross-correlation learns them one at a time, in order of eigenvalue, and ends at a top spectral solution, which is exactly a minimum-norm zero-loss solution: kernel PCA on K_Γ | Simon et al. (2023), [LIT-242](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-242.md), read in [NOTE-741](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-741.md). For L = ‖C − I‖²_F with λ = 1, no batch norm and C symmetrized by hand, a linear model from aligned initialization learns mode j at τ_j ≈ −log(s_j(0)²γ_j)/(8γ_j) (Prop. 4.1, proved), the top spectral solutions are exactly the minimum-norm zero-loss ones (Prop. 4.3), and the kernel version is kernel PCA on K_Γ (Prop. 5.1). Generic small initialization is covered by an informal derivation only. The operator is built from the model's kernel and the sample pairs, not from the positive-pair density ratio, and the stepwise growth seen in ResNets under SimCLR and VICReg is an experiment, not a consequence. | Active |
| [THEORY-230](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-230.md) v2 | The Fisher–Rao geometry of a language model's next-token laws over a set of contexts is a function of those laws alone, so models with identical laws share it, while activation geometry changes under invertible reparameterizations of the hidden layer that leave outputs unchanged; in Picozzi's ten transformer, state-space and recurrent models it agreed at a mean rank correlation of 0.88 against 0.62 for activation geometry, and about 9% of the top eigenvector overlap exceeded a null matched to the shared laws | Picozzi (2026), [LIT-936](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-936.md), read in [NOTE-755](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-755.md), a single-author v1 preprint with code on request. The matrix of Fisher–Rao distances between a model's next-token laws on a context battery is invariant to every output-preserving reparameterization, while activation geometry has a GL(d) gauge (Prop. 1); two models with identical outputs can have hidden geometries that rank-correlate at −4/17 (Prop. 3). Over ten transformer, state-space and recurrent models the mean rank agreement is 0.88 against 0.62 for mid-layer activations. Convergence is proved only as a consequence of each model's excess risk to a common law, and that bound is vacuous on real models. Against a law-matched null, about 9% of the top-six eigenvector overlap is shared beyond the laws. Promoted on 2026-10-20. Replication and a test that varies the law are QUESTION-216. | Active |
| [THEORY-233](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-233.md) v2 | CKA and normalized Bures similarity are the Euclidean and the Bures comparison of normalized kernels, and each bounds the other only within a factor set by the kernels' ranks, so agreement in one does not carry to the other with a dimension-free constant | Harvey, Larsen & Williams (2023), [LIT-250](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-250.md), §5 and App. A.3, read in [NOTE-753](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-753.md). CKA = 1 − ½‖K_X/‖K_X‖_F − K_Y/‖K_Y‖_F‖²_F, while NBS = 1 − ½B²(K_X/Tr K_X, K_Y/Tr K_Y), with B the Bures distance. They induce the same topology, but CKA/√(r(K_X)r(K_Y)) ≤ NBS² ≤ min[r(K_X), r(K_Y)]·CKA, saturated at rank 1. NBS bounds CKA of the square-root kernels, with equality for commuting kernels. Linear kernels only, and the discrepancy is illustrated on Wishart samples, not trained networks. | Active |
| [THEORY-234](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-234.md) v2 | Two softmax next-token predictors induce the same distribution exactly when their embeddings and unembeddings are related by an invertible linear map on the subspaces that enter the logits, with arbitrary distortion off them, so a linear relational property is shared by all such models or none when it lies in those subspaces, and can fail to be shared otherwise | Marconato et al. (2024), [LIT-950](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-950.md), read in [NOTE-746](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-746.md). For p(y\|s) ∝ exp(f(s)ᵀg(y)) on a shared vocabulary, p_{f,g} = p_{f̃,g̃} iff the models are extended-linearly equivalent: invertible linear maps between the subspaces M and N that enter the logits, at any dimensions and without the diversity condition (Thm 5). The dimension of M is then a property of the distribution. Relational linearity, linear subspaces and linear probing hold in all equivalent models or none when Γ ⊆ N and Γ_q ⊆ M (Thm 14), and parallelism is shared only within N (Thm 15). Exact equality of distributions only, and no experiments. | Active |
| [THEORY-236](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-236.md) v2 | A representational similarity index that is invariant to every invertible linear map takes the same value on all representations whose rank equals the number of examples | Kornblith, Norouzi, Lee & Hinton (2019), [LIT-254](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-254.md), Theorem 1, read in [NOTE-743](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-743.md). If s(X, Z) = s(XA, Z) for every invertible A, and rank(X) = rank(Y) = n, then s(X, Z) = s(Y, Z): any two full-row-rank representations of the same n examples are related by an invertible linear map. So when width reaches the number of examples, an index with that invariance, such as CCA, says nothing. The theorem fixes no group; the paper's case for orthogonal invariance plus isotropic scaling is an argument from training dynamics, not a consequence of it. | Active |
| [THEORY-237](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-237.md) v3 | The critic-based variational lower bounds on mutual information, Donsker–Varadhan, NWJ, MINE's and InfoNCE, are relaxations of one unnormalized Barber–Agakov bound, and, when the joint and the product of the marginals are mutually absolutely continuous, each attains its supremum over critics only at a critic equal to the log density ratio up to a term its normalization leaves free, where every bound but InfoNCE equals the mutual information | Poole, Ozair, van den Oord, Alemi & Tucker (2019), [LIT-246](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-246.md), read in [NOTE-739](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-739.md). Writing q(x\|y) = p(x)e^f/Z(y) in Barber and Agakov's bound gives I_UBA, tight at f = log p(y\|x) + c(y). Jensen gives Donsker–Varadhan, a tangent bound on the log gives TUBA and NWJ (unique optimal critic 1 + log p(x\|y)/p(x)), and NWJ applied to a K-sample problem with the batch mean as normalizer gives InfoNCE. MINE's bias-corrected gradient is the exact gradient of TUBA. A Monte-Carlo DV estimate is neither an upper nor a lower bound. The InfoNCE optimum is cited, not derived, in the source (the record derives it, note of 2026-10-19), and the bias–variance comparisons are on toys. | Active |
| [THEORY-238](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-238.md) v3 | The expected generalization error of an encoder–decoder learner is bounded by the encoder alone, through the KL divergence of its train-and-ghost latents to a prior symmetric under label-preserving permutations, for any decoder; and under lossy compression the bound can stay finite for deterministic continuous encoders, whose lossless bound is infinite | Sefidgaran, Zaidi & Krasnowski (2023), [LIT-245](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-245.md), read in [NOTE-742](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-742.md). Theorem 4: E[gen] ≤ inf 2√((2·MDL + K + 2)/n) + ε, where MDL is the expected KL of the joint law of the latents of the training set and an independent ghost set to any prior invariant under label-preserving permutations, and ε is the distortion allowed by lossy compression. It holds for any decoder. With a product prior it reduces to sample-wise mutual information. The bound is never evaluated, the prior may depend on unseen ghost data, and a 2√((K+2)/n) floor remains. It does not prove that I(X;U) cannot bound generalization. | Active |
| [THEORY-239](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-239.md) v3 | For any joint law of an input and a context, symmetric or not, the top-d left singular functions of the conditional-expectation operator attain the minimum, over d-dimensional spans, of worst-case linear-probe approximation error over tasks of compatibility at least 1 − ε, namely (s₁² − (1 − ε)²)/(s₁² − s²_{d+1}) when s_{d+1} < 1 − ε ≤ s₁, though other spans can tie | Zhai (2025), [LIT-975](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-975.md), read in [NOTE-770](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-770.md): Lemma 1.4, Theorem 3.2 and Theorem 3.4 with App. B. The operator g ↦ E[g(A)\|X] runs from L²(P_A) to L²(P_X) and is never assumed self-adjoint; its singular value decomposition comes from composing it with its adjoint. The guarantee is for linear probes and approximation error at the population level only. The thesis never works a non-reversible kernel on one space; the note of 2026-10-19 works a three-state one. It says nothing of what a trained network reaches. | Active |
| [THEORY-241](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-241.md) | Fitting the same function in the same architecture does not fix the internal decomposition: SGD reproduces three Picbreeder images from random weights without the reuse and factoring of the evolved networks, and perturbing its weights breaks the regularities that perturbing the evolved networks' weights preserves | Kumar, Clune, Lehman & Stanley (2025), [LIT-944](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-944.md), read in [NOTE-771](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-771.md). For the skull, butterfly and apple CPPNs, SGD in the layerized evolved architecture fits the image, the network's whole function on the grid. It shows no reuse of the symmetric parts, and single-weight and random-direction sweeps distort the output, where the evolved networks' sweeps vary it meaningfully. Qualitative, curated and three images. The paper's account of why, the order of discovery in open-ended search, and its extension to large models are conjecture. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-243](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-243.md) v3 | In the three-unit identity network x ↦ x(1, 0, 1) ↦ (0, 2, 1)·h, aligning the input with the third unit and aligning it with the direction (h₁ + h₂)/√2, two alignments related by an orthogonal change of basis, pass every interchange intervention on the input equally, so interchange interventions on that variable alone do not fix which internal direction mediates it | Wu et al. (2024), [LIT-961](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-961.md), Appendix A, and Makelov et al. (2023), [LIT-968](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-968.md), Appendix A.3 and §8, read in [NOTE-809](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-809.md) and [NOTE-782](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-782.md). Both rotate the same three-unit identity network. The input aligns with h₃ in one basis and with (h₁ + h₂)/√2 in the other, equally well under interchange interventions on the input (re-derived 2026-10-20). The reply says intervening on further variables separates them; that was not checked. Makelov et al. rest their verdict on component boundaries; the reply rests its on the interventions performed. Shown exactly for one constructed network only; whether trained networks have such ties is open (QUESTION-234). | Active |
| [THEORY-246](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-246.md) v2 | Among ResNet-50s trained on ImageNet with nine objectives and stopped early, seven of which beat softmax cross-entropy's top-1 by up to 0.9 points, fixed penultimate features with more class separation transfer worse by linear probe to datasets whose classes are mostly not ImageNet's (Spearman ρ = −0.93 across the nine; mean accuracy 75.9% for softmax to 48.3% for squared error), and within cosine softmax a higher temperature raises separation and lowers that accuracy; the objectives' representations differ mainly in the last third of the network, and full fine-tuning brings mean transfer to within 1.3 points across them | Kornblith, Chen, Lee & Norouzi (2021), [LIT-1044](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1044.md), read in [NOTE-762](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-762.md). Across nine objectives for ResNet-50 on ImageNet, penultimate class separation R² runs from 0.349 (softmax) to 0.845 (squared error), Papyan's Tr(Σ_W Σ_B†)/C from 21.2 to 0.33, and mean linear transfer to eight new-class datasets falls with R² (Spearman ρ = −0.93), from 75.9% to 48.3%. Cosine-softmax temperature raises R² from 0.24 to 0.77 and lowers transfer from 76.0% to 58.9%. CKA puts the differences in the last third of the network; fine-tuning erases them. The cost is for new classes: relearning the training classes, more separation helps. Networks early-stopped near 92% training accuracy; one dataset; correlational across losses. Promoted 2026-10-20 on this one study (ADR-047 v3), narrowed to what it measured. | Active |
| [THEORY-251](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-251.md) | In few-shot classification by a base language model, failures from the choice of examples or from relabelled categories leave the class representations separable and fail at the vocabulary readout | Kirsanov et al. (2025), [LIT-946](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-946.md), read in [NOTE-789](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-789.md): at five demonstrations, accuracy across draws of examples runs from below 0.1 to about 0.6 while final-layer manifold capacity barely moves, and consistently swapped labels fail while capacity matches gold labels. The readout explanation is inferred from that dissociation, not measured; base Llama-3.1-8B and Gemma-2-2B, mostly synthetic data. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-256](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-256.md) v3 | When a sequence generator's latent dynamics factor as a tensor product, its predictive state embeds losslessly and linearly in orthogonal per-factor subspaces of total dimension Σ(d_n − 1); 4-layer GPT-2-style transformers trained by next-token prediction on five Mess3 and Bloch Walk factors settle near that dimension, in per-factor subspaces that are linearly independent and approximately orthogonal in their leading components, and under the token noise tested reach it first even when noise makes it lossy | Shai et al. (2026), [LIT-986](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-986.md), read in [NOTE-758](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-758.md). The lossless embedding is an elementary theorem (Prop. 2.2, Thm 2.3, App. A). | [THEORY-264](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-264.md) | A task given by demonstrations and the same task given by an instruction are carried in a language model by mostly different attention heads, so function vectors find no common task representation across the two presentations | Davidson et al. (NeurIPS 2025), [LIT-942](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-942.md), read in [NOTE-803](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-803.md): 4 to 7 of the top 20 function-vector heads are shared between the two forms in twelve Llama and OLMo models, the two vectors add, and swapping heads and activations between them costs accuracy. | [THEORY-269](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-269.md) | In OLMo-1B, OLMo-7B and GPT-J, whether a factual relation is computed by an affine map from subject to object representation tracks how often its subjects and objects co-occur in pretraining, with mean causality above 0.9 beyond about 4.4k, 2.0k and 1.1k co-occurrences respectively, whenever in training that count is reached | Merullo, Smith, Wiegreffe and Elazar (2025), [LIT-972](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-972.md), read in full in [NOTE-786](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-786.md). 24 factual relations, three models, eight OLMo-7B checkpoints; r = 0.82 between LRE causality and mean subject–object co-occurrence, above either term's frequency alone. Correlational by the authors' own statement. The linear objects are per-relation affine maps between hidden states, not attribute directions. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-271](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-271.md) v2 | In a toy subject–verb–object corpus whose eight subjects carry every combination of three binary aspects, the subjects' raw co-occurrence rows form a parallelepiped if and only if, for each object, its four sentences are equally probable; any other sentence distribution breaks it | Torii, Maeda and Hidaka (2024), [LIT-977](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-977.md), Theorem 1 (§5.5), read in full in [NOTE-781](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-781.md). Exact shapes, raw counts, one design, and independent aspects that make the concept lattice Boolean. | [THEORY-274](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-274.md) | Sequence models trained only on a graph's edge bigrams store it as a global embedding geometry, not as a lookup, although the lookup is expressible, found faster and no less succinct; in a wide two-layer weight-tied model the geometry is the top Laplacian eigenspace, reached by cross-entropy training without a rank bottleneck, regularization or multi-hop supervision | Noroozizadeh, Nagarajan, Rosenfeld & Kumar (2025), [LIT-995](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-995.md), read in [NOTE-800](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-800.md). | [THEORY-278](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-278.md) v3 | Under MSE loss, in Han, Papyan and Donoho's VGG, ResNet and DenseNet runs on five balanced ten-class datasets, the trained classifier stays near the least-squares classifier for its own features from an early epoch; and on that central path, for unconstrained features continually renormalized to identity within-class covariance and without weight decay, gradient flow drives the class-separation singular values to infinity at equal rates, which in that model is neural collapse | Han, Papyan & Donoho (2021), [LIT-974](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-974.md), read in [NOTE-783](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-783.md). MSE loss splits exactly into a least-squares term and a non-negative deviation term, and the deviation becomes negligible early in training in 15 dataset–network cells. On that central path, with λ = 0, the loss is ½ Σ 1/(ω_j² + C) in the singular values of Σ_W^(−1/2)M̃. Under a flow that re-whitens the features after every step, each ω_j grows as (4t/N)^(1/4), and their ratios tend to 1. That is NC1 and NC2, and NC3–NC4 follow. Not shown: that ordinary training is this flow, or anything for cross-entropy or with weight decay. | Active |
| [THEORY-279](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-279.md) v2 | Early in training, image classifiers and language models act on the low-order statistics of their inputs, first-order before second-order, and later lose that sensitivity as they come to use higher-order structure | Belrose et al. (2024, ICML), [LIT-952](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-952.md), read in [NOTE-777](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-777.md). Over training, ConvNeXt V2, Swin V2 and RegNet-Y on five small image datasets are probed with images whose class means or covariances are grafted from another class, and with maximum-entropy samples that keep only those statistics. Accuracy on these rises and then falls, often below chance. Pythia fits unigram-sampled text before bigram-sampled text. The ordering is empirical and covers orders one and two. The Taylor argument that motivates it is a heuristic, and the paper does not measure an ordered sequence beyond second order. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-281](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-281.md) v2 | Perfect concept erasure caps what a representation can keep at the information not about the concept: for X of finite support, if Z is independent of A then I(Z;X) is at most H(X\|A), and a deterministic erasure reaches that cap only when the concept groups' distributions are permutations of one another | Chowdhury et al. (2025), [LIT-963](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-963.md), read in full in [NOTE-820](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-820.md). The cap (Lemma 3.3) is a two-line chain-rule argument that needs only the Markov condition A → X → Z. The permutation condition is proved necessary and sufficient for deterministic maps (Appendices A.3 and A.4), with finite supports and disjoint groups. The paper's further statement, that the cap cannot be reached when the groups are not permutations, is false for stochastic maps, which reach it for any finite distributions with disjoint supports. | Active |
| [THEORY-282](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-282.md) v2 | A subspace intervention can reproduce the output effect of changing a variable without localizing it, by pairing a direction that varies with the variable but cannot reach the output with one that can reach the output but does not vary on the data | Makelov, Lange and Nanda (2023), [LIT-968](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-968.md), read in [NOTE-782](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-782.md). The reply ([LIT-961](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-961.md)) contests the label, not the measurements. | Active |
| [THEORY-283](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-283.md) v2 | For a hierarchical multi-index target with isotropic Gaussian inputs and even, separable links, direction k becomes weakly recoverable by the Bayes-optimal estimator at a sample count proportional to its squared weight to the power minus one, so features emerge one at a time through sharp spectral transitions in the number of samples; a target-agnostic spectral estimator attains the thresholds and the optimal weighted error, and a two-layer network whose first layer is that estimator, with a ridge readout, attains them in excess risk | Defilippis, Krzakala, Loureiro and Maillard (2026), [LIT-940](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-940.md), read in [NOTE-805](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-805.md). Take x ~ N(0, I/d), n = αd, and f⋆ = Σ a_k g_k(⟨w_k, x⟩) with even links of generative exponent two and a_k ~ k^(−γ). Direction k is weakly recoverable at α_k = Θ(a_k^(−2)) (Thm. 3.2). The optimal weighted error is Θ(α^(−1+1/(2γ))) until α ≍ m⋆^(2γ). The spectral estimator on Σ T(y_i)x_ix_iᵀ attains both (Thm. 3.6). The cascade is in the number of samples, not in training time. The network result is for a spectral first layer plus a ridge readout, not gradient descent. | Active |
| [THEORY-284](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-284.md) v2 | If a feature's values form a compact metric space carried continuously and injectively onto the unit sphere, and cosine similarity is locally a C² decreasing function of squared feature distance, then every path on the representation manifold is √(−2g′(0)) times as long as the feature path it images, so on-manifold shortest paths recover the feature's intrinsic length metric up to one scale; a homeomorphism alone does not fix it | Modell, Rubin-Delanchy & Whiteley (2025), [LIT-935](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-935.md), Theorem 1, read in [NOTE-802](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-802.md). Under Hypothesis 1 (continuous injective ϕ_f from a compact feature space to the sphere) and Hypothesis 2 (CosSim = g(d²) locally, g ∈ C², g′(0) < 0), path lengths scale by √(−2g′(0)). So geodesics on the representation measure the feature, without knowing g. Both hypotheses are assumed, not derived from training. GPT-2's years are homeomorphic to both a linear and a logarithmic scale, and only the metric test told them apart. | Active |
| [THEORY-286](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-286.md) v2 | Under class imbalance the last-layer geometry that unregularized cross-entropy prefers is not the simplex ETF but simplex-encoded-label interpolation: the logits equal the simplex-encoded labels, the classifier and embedding Gram matrices come from that matrix's SVD, any finite weight decay changes the geometry, and training approaches it more slowly as imbalance grows | Thrampoulidis et al. (2022), [LIT-994](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-994.md), read in [NOTE-764](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-764.md). For the unconstrained-features max-margin problem under STEP imbalance, every solution has logits ŴᵀĤ = Ẑ (one-hot minus 1/k), ĤᵀĤ = UΛUᵀ and ŴᵀŴ = VΛVᵀ from Ẑ's SVD (Theorem 1). | [THEORY-287](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-287.md) | Internal variables located by interchange intervention as mediating a language model's in-distribution behaviour predict whether its outputs stay correct under shifts that keep the task's mechanism better than output confidence or probes of the rest of the representation | Huang, Tao, Icard, Yang and Potts (2025), [LIT-987](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-987.md), read in [NOTE-765](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-765.md). In Llama-3-8B-Instruct over five tasks and ten shifts, counterfactual simulation is best on 8 of 10; a probe of the located variable beats a probe of its orthogonal complement on 7 of 10. Interchange accuracy and predictive power rise together only until accuracy nears 1. | [THEORY-288](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-288.md) v2 | In small CIFAR and MNIST autoencoders whose only basis-privileging primitive is the activation function, elementwise tanh and Leaky-ReLU concentrate latent representations into narrow beams arranged by the activation's discrete symmetry group, even in layers no activation precedes, while their orthogonally equivariant radial counterparts leave them spread, so axis-aligned discreteness there comes from the primitive, not the task | Bird (2025, v4 2026), [LIT-976](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-976.md), read in [NOTE-759](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-759.md). Autoencoders of width 12–32 and up to three hidden blocks on CIFAR and MNIST, with rotation-equivariant affine maps, initialisation and optimiser. Elementwise tanh (B_n) and Leaky-ReLU (S_n) give beams along or against the basis, or on the ±1 diagonal, and radial tanh and Leaky-ReLU (O(n)) do not. The evidence is density plots, five seeds a condition, with no statistic. The downstream claims, that this causes grandmother neurons, superposition and neural collapse, are untested. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-292](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-292.md) | In CNN image classifiers, concept directions fitted one concept at a time align for attributes that co-occur in the labels, yet a joint fit finds mutually orthogonal directions that still separate each concept with little loss of AUROC, so the alignment is a property of the separate fits and not forced by the representation | Erogullari, Lapuschkin, Samek and Pahde (2025), [LIT-937](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-937.md), read in full in [NOTE-816](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-816.md). AUROC is "largely preserved" by the paper's account, with no values in the text and no error bars. It does not say the model's own axes are orthogonal, and it says nothing about attributes that imply one another. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-294](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-294.md) v3 | For a wide two-layer ReLU network with zero bias on one-dimensional data whose two classes lie on opposite sides of the origin, the tangent kernel is a constant multiple of the initialization kernel, so lazy training leaves the within-class variability of its features, NC1, where initialization put it | Kothapalli & Tirer (2024), [LIT-985](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-985.md), read in [NOTE-774](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-774.md). NC1 = tr Σ_W / tr Σ_B of kernel-defined features is a ratio of linear functionals of the kernel matrix (Theorem 4.1). For one-dimensional data, two classes on opposite sides of the origin and zero bias, the ReLU tangent kernel of a wide two-layer net is a constant multiple of the NNGP kernel, so NC1 is the same (Theorem 5.1, re-derived). In higher dimensions it is measured no lower, and for ReLU higher; whether lazy training leaves NC1 in place there is [QUESTION-192](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-192.md). The inference that collapse requires feature learning is the reading's, not proved. | Active |
| [THEORY-299](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-299.md) v2 | Structured and translational knowledge-graph embeddings are 0-cochains of a cellular sheaf of vector spaces pulled back from the schema, each triple scored by a norm of the coboundary on its edge and, in the squared-Euclidean form, the whole graph by the sheaf Laplacian; since the zero cochain is always a global section, what they learn is a contrastive margin, not the existence of a section | Gebhart, Hansen and Schrater (2021; AISTATS 2023), [LIT-232](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-232.md), §4 and Appendices A and C, read in [NOTE-843](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-843.md). A direct identification, covering Structured Embedding, the Unstructured Model, TransE, TransR and RotatE and not bilinear models. That existence of a section is trivial here, and that the only gluing question is whether fixed data extend, is the paper's own remark taken further by the record; it is what separates this use of sheaves from the contextuality line. | Active |
| [THEORY-301](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-301.md) v2 | The Procrustes distance between regularization-normalized representations and their average linear-decoding distance bound each other only through the participation ratio of the kernel difference: a small Procrustes distance forces a small decoding distance, but not conversely | Harvey, Lipshutz & Williams (2024), [LIT-257](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-257.md), Proposition 3 and App. A.1, read in [NOTE-834](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-834.md). With K_X = XG(X)⁻¹Xᵀ/M, α = Tr K_X, β = Tr K_Y and R_Δ the participation ratio of K_X − K_Y, P⁴/R_Δ ≤ E‖Xw* − Yv*‖² ≤ (2(α + β)P² − P⁴)/R_Δ for targets with E[zzᵀ] = I. The Procrustes–Bures equivalence is imported from [LIT-250](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-250.md). Kernels with orthogonal supports show the converse fails: Procrustes distance maximal, decoding distance as small as 2/r. Finite samples, linear readouts only. | Active |
| [THEORY-305](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-305.md) v2 | SimCLR's InfoNCE loss, over all n objects with a Gaussian kernel on the unit sphere, equals a graph-Laplacian quadratic form on the augmentation matrix plus the log of InfoNCE's normalizers, which is spectral clustering only in a sense that admits any regularizer and does not make the minimizer the Laplacian's eigenvectors | Tan, Zhang, Yang & Yuan (2023, ICLR 2024), [LIT-227](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-227.md), read in [NOTE-846](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-846.md): Theorem 3.1 and its proof (App. A), Lemma 2.5 and Definition 2.7. The identity between objectives is exact on a finite object set with symmetric π. The paper's "spectral clustering" is any Laplacian form plus any regularizer; it names no minimizer and no population optimum, so it supports neither an eigenvector reading of InfoNCE nor the density-ratio optimum of [THEORY-001](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-001.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-306](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-306.md) v3 | MSN's objective penalizes unequal cluster sizes explicitly and SwAV's enforces equal sizes, and in one study with mini-batches of two to eight ImageNet classes, SimCLR, MSN and VICReg lost 11 to 18 points of ImageNet linear accuracy while MAE and data2vec lost under one | Assran et al. (2022), [LIT-231](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-231.md), §§3–5 and Appendix C, read in [NOTE-850](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-850.md). The prior is explicit in MSN's loss (a KL to uniform over mean cluster assignments) and in SwAV's equipartition constraint. For VICReg it rests on an informal reduction of a simplified loss to K-means and on K-means's cited tendency to equal clusters, and for SimCLR on a cited equivalence, so the title claims the prior for MSN and SwAV only. The effect is shown with batches of two to eight ImageNet classes, one run per cell, not with natural long tails; the open half is QUESTION-171. | Active |
| [THEORY-312](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-312.md) v2 | The large-batch InfoNCE loss is the negative HSIC between representations and image identity plus a nonnegative log-mean-exp of the centred critic, so it bounds a kernel dependence loss from above | Li, Pogodin, Sutherland & Gretton (2021), [LIT-248](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-248.md), eq. 28 and Theorem B.1, read in [NOTE-830](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-830.md). On a finite dataset of N images with one-hot identity labels, the large-batch InfoNCE loss equals −HSIC(Z,Y) + E_Z log E_Z′ exp(k − μ₁) exactly. The second term is nonnegative by Jensen (the record's step), and for a bounded kernel it is at least γHSIC(Z,Z) less a second-order remainder (Theorem B.1, printed with the remainder's sign reversed). It does not say InfoNCE is HSIC, and it says nothing of the finite-batch estimator. | Active |
| [THEORY-319](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-319.md) v2 | When two views are redundant for a label, the predictor that infers one view from the other is within εX + 2√(εXεZ) + εZ of the Bayes predictor in mean squared error, and it is linear in the contrastive density ratio, so for a bounded label and a square-integrable ratio a linear readout of m random evaluations of the exact ratio approaches it at rate 1/m, with no symmetry between the views required | Tosh, Krishnamurthy & Hsu (2021), [LIT-251](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-251.md), read in [NOTE-841](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-841.md): Lemma 1, §2.3–2.4, Lemma 2 and Theorem 3. The label enters only through how redundant the views are about it; the representation is the density ratio p(x,z)/(p(x)p(z)), learned without labels. Population level. The error-propagation results need a uniform bound on the ratio, and the low-dimensional direct embeddings are shown to exist, not to be reached. | Active |
| [THEORY-320](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-320.md) v2 | In a spectral contrastive graph that joins labelled known classes to unlabelled data, a novel labelling's linear-probe residual is exactly its part outside the top eigenspace that the labelled rows of the discarded eigenvectors cannot absorb, so which partition of the unlabelled data is discovered depends on the known classes: ones sharing the target's attribute can remove the residual, and ones sharing a rival attribute can raise it | Sun, Shi, Liang & Li (2023), [LIT-235](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-235.md), read in [NOTE-833](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-833.md). In a one-sample-per-kind toy, a known class sharing colour makes a colour labelling recoverable, and one sharing shape makes it worse than none (Lemma 5.4). The general error bound (Theorem 5.6) is approximate and pools all known classes into one block, and is not part of this account. Nothing here is about trained networks. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-420](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-420.md) | In trained transformers, zeroing a decile of a weight matrix's singular values does damage that falls monotonically with their size in square matrices, whose random-matrix null reaches zero, but not in rectangular ones, whose null has a positive lower edge: there the smallest decile is never the least damaging and can be among the most | Staats, Thamm & Rosenow (2024), [LIT-856](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-856.md), read in [NOTE-659](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-659.md). Freshly initialised matrices of BERT, Pythia and Llama follow the Marchenko–Pastur law; trained ones depart from it above the bulk, and, in rectangular matrices only, below it. Zeroing Llama-3 8B's smallest Down-Projection decile leaves 2.0% on GSM8K from 43.2%, worse than every decile but the largest, while the same decile of the square Attention-Output leaves 40.0%. | [THEORY-421](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-421.md) v2 | In HGCN embeddings of two synthetic 3-ary trees trained for link prediction or node classification, distance from the origin is only a partial reading of hierarchical level: the root is not innermost (distance 1.8–3.3 against a minimum of 1.2–2.4) and level order is recovered for 69–75% of node pairs; a loss built only on pairwise distances leaves the origin arbitrary | Yang, Zhou, Ying, Chen & King (2023), [LIT-871](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-871.md), read in [NOTE-669](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-669.md). On two synthetic 3-ary trees of eight levels, HGCN leaves the root at hyperbolic distance 1.8–3.3 from the origin where the minimum is 1.2–2.4, the distances are roughly normal rather than leaf-heavy, and radius orders true levels for 69–75% of 5,000 random pairs. Recentring on the centroid plus an outward push raises that to 75–84%. The diagnosis rests on one architecture, two synthetic trees and one table without variance, and the paper does not separate a real failure to order levels from the origin's arbitrariness under losses that see only pairwise distances. | Active |
| [THEORY-439](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-439.md) | Given the same few demonstrations, temporarily updating a language model's weights on them and then conditioning beats conditioning alone, most on tasks with structural rules or distribution shift and most when the update is trained in the in-context format: for models of 1–8B parameters, examples used as context and the same examples used as a training signal are not interchangeable | Akyürek et al. (2024; ICML 2025), [LIT-796](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-796.md), read in [NOTE-637](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-637.md). On BIG-Bench Hard with Llama 3.1 8B and 10 demonstrations over five seeds, zero-shot 40.9%, in-context 50.5%, per-task LoRA test-time training then in-context 57.8%; 12 of 27 tasks gain at least 2 points, and Boolean expressions falls. Training the update on leave-one-out in-context tasks beats training on bare pairs (57.8% against 51.5%). The update is discarded after each task, so it is as transient as a context. It is two benchmarks and one model family, and which task property predicts the gain is open. | Active |
| [THEORY-445](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-445.md) | A network built from group correlations over a discrete split group of plane symmetries, pointwise nonlinearities and coset pooling is equivariant to that group by construction, through the regular representation alone: the group is fixed before training and built into the weight sharing, not found in the data | Cohen & Welling (2016), [LIT-314](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-314.md), read in [NOTE-288](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-288.md). G-correlation commutes with the left action of G by the change of variables h → uh (eq. 12), and so do pointwise nonlinearities and pooling over cosets, up to edge effects and for rotations that are symmetries of the grid. Matched-parameter p4 and p4m layers lowered rotated-MNIST error from 5.03% to 2.28% and plain-CIFAR10 error from 9.45% to 6.46%. The paper uses no irreducible representations, characters or Fourier analysis, learns nothing about which symmetry the data have, and does not separate the effect of equivariance from the changed channel structure. | Active |
| [THEORY-478](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-478.md) v2 | If the diffusion densities' Hellinger distances obey a Hölder bound with exponent θ in d_T / t^(1/β) and are bounded below once d_T exceeds a multiple of t^(1/β), then for 0 < α < θ/β summing scale-weighted hyperbolic distances between diffusion densities over dyadic times gives a distance two-sided equivalent, up to constants, to min{1, d_T^(αβ)} for pairs above the finest scale: it keeps the tree's neighbourhoods and not its global distances; whether a tree's heat kernel, or sampled data, meets the bounds, and with which θ, is not shown | Lin, Coifman, Mishne & Talmon (2023), [LIT-870](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-870.md), read in [NOTE-675](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-675.md). The hyperbolic diffusion distance is equivalent to min{1, d_T^(2α)} for 0 < α < 1/2 (Proposition C.4), under heat-kernel bounds on the tree that are cited rather than proved; one Hölder step holds only for d_T ≥ 1, and repaired, the reader finds the admissible range halves. Pairs beyond a radius are only known to be far, which matches the method's best mean average precision and its higher distortion than hyperbolic MDS on five graph benchmarks. A Euclidean distance on the same multiscale features does far worse. | Active |
| [THEORY-481](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-481.md) v2 | A linear-attention layer trained on in-context regression learns as a two-layer linear network does: when tasks share the input covariance's eigenbasis and the weights stay aligned with it, then in the long-context limit each input mode is learned on its own logistic curve whose timescale falls with the square of its variance, so learning is staged by the input spectrum, and the layer converges to a preconditioned estimator; at finite context length the modes decouple exactly only when inputs are isotropic, and otherwise couple at order 1/N | Mainali & Teixeira (2025), [LIT-859](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-859.md), read in [NOTE-658](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-658.md). The prediction of one linear-attention layer reduces to p₂ W Σ̂_x q₁ x_q, a product of two learned factors, so averaged gradient flow decouples into modes with τ_α dp_α/dt = q_α(1 − p_α q_α s^∞_α) and τ_α = (ηP s_α²)⁻¹, logistic from a balanced start. The fixed point ŷ = W Σ̂_x [((N+1)/N)Σ_x + (Tr Σ_x/N)I]⁻¹ x_q is the one Ahn et al. and Zhang, Frei & Bartlett found; the trajectory is new. The decoupling into independent modes is exact as N → ∞. At finite N it holds only for isotropic inputs with equal modes: the paper commutes the non-diagonal empirical covariance at (A71) and (A73), and the correct Wishart moment couples the modes at order 1/N. Alignment of the weights with the data's eigenbasis is assumed throughout, the null blocks vanish only in expectation over tasks, and the transfer to non-linear transformers is timing coincidences. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-496](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-496.md) | In few-shot classification and multiple choice by language models up to 175B parameters, whether each demonstration's label is correct contributes little to the gain over zero-shot, while the distribution of the inputs, the label space and the paired format carry most of it | Min et al. (2022), [LIT-814](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-814.md), read in [NOTE-607](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-607.md). With k = 16 demonstrations, labels drawn at random from the correct label set cost 0–5 points against gold labels (2.6 on classification, 1.7 on multiple choice on average) across twelve model–inference combinations and 26 datasets. Out-of-distribution inputs, random English words as labels, or breaking the input–label pairing each cost far more. The random labels always come from the right label set, gaps reach about 14 points on single datasets, and the authors' reading that the models learn no new correspondence at test time is untested on tasks pretraining cannot have taught. | Active |
| [THEORY-503](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-503.md) | The nearest rank-r matrix to a real matrix in the least-squares norm keeps its r largest singular values and zeroes the rest; it is unique when the r-th and (r+1)-th singular values differ, its squared error is the sum of the dropped squares, and the singular-vector factors that build it are not unique | Eckart & Young (1936), [LIT-330](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-330.md), read in full in [NOTE-301](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-301.md), which checked the error bound. The argument is first-order stationarity on the orthogonal group plus two cited theorems (the SVD and a simultaneous-SVD criterion), and assumes a minimiser exists. Only the Frobenius norm and real matrices are covered. Uniqueness is of the approximating matrix, under a spectral gap, never of the factors; the paper's last section argues the canonic components cannot be read straightforwardly as psychological factors. | Active |
| [THEORY-504](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-504.md) v2 | In the Gemma Scope sparse autoencoders on Gemma 2, the two fidelity measures disagree by site: residual-stream autoencoders cost more next-token loss than MLP or attention ones at comparable fraction of variance unexplained, and base-model autoencoders transfer to the instruction-tuned model by loss more than by variance explained | Lieberum et al. (2024), [LIT-611](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-611.md), read in [NOTE-482](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-482.md). Across every layer and sublayer of Gemma 2 2B and 9B, JumpReLU autoencoders on the residual stream raise the language model's loss more, when spliced in, than MLP and attention autoencoders whose FVU is about the same; and autoencoders trained on the base model lose little loss on instruction-tuned rollouts while showing a larger FVU gap. The authors' explanations (the residual stream is the bottleneck; fine-tuning re-weights old features) are conjectures, and the authors say no agreed metric of autoencoder quality exists. | Active |
| [THEORY-565](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-565.md) v2 | From a symmetric, positivity-preserving, positive semi-definite affinity, the normalized Markov operator is conjugate to a symmetric one, so its leading eigenfunctions scaled by powers of their eigenvalues embed the data with Euclidean distance equal to diffusion distance, and a density-corrected normalization recovers the Laplace–Beltrami operator independently of how the data were sampled | Coifman et al. (2005), [LIT-981](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-981.md), skimmed in [NOTE-784](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-784.md) from extracted text whose displayed equations were not visible. The construction and the embedding are standard. The convergence theorem and the α-family are stated without proof, which is deferred to a companion paper. [NOTE-784](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-784.md) filed no THEORY for those reasons. It is filed Proposed on the owner's ruling that a well-established result may rest on a skim when it is not wrong as stated. Self-adjointness comes from the kernel's symmetry, and the paper's "directed diffusion" is anisotropic, not a non-reversible chain. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-566](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-566.md) v2 | In Ganea et al.'s hyperbolic neural networks, linear maps and nonlinearities are Euclidean ones read through the chart at the origin, so a stack of them without biases is a Euclidean network conjugated by that chart, and the curvature acts only through the bias translations and the distance-based output layer | Ganea, Bécigneul & Hofmann (2018), [LIT-879](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-879.md), read in [NOTE-686](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-686.md), which checked the closed forms numerically. Möbius layers are defined as exp₀ ∘ f ∘ log₀, so any composition of them is exp₀ ∘ (the Euclidean composition) ∘ log₀, as the paper notes; only the Möbius bias, which is parallel transport from the origin followed by the exponential map, and the hyperbolic logistic regression's distances to geodesic hyperplanes are not absorbed by the chart. The structural fact is proved; that the networks' gains, confined to a synthetic task and to separating WordNet subtrees in low-dimensional Poincaré embeddings, come from those two operations is this record's inference. [NOTE-686](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-686.md) filed no THEORY. | Active |
| [THEORY-640](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-640.md) | Measured as mutual 10-nearest-neighbour overlap, competent vision models agree more with one another and better language models agree more with vision models, but the cross-modal score reaches only 0.16 of a possible 1, is the maximum over all layer pairs, and was adopted after a global kernel metric showed only a very weak trend | Huh, Cheung, Wang & Isola (2024), [LIT-302](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-302.md), read in [NOTE-286](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-286.md). Across 78 vision models, those solving more VTAB tasks agree more in mutual k-nearest-neighbour structure; language models with lower bits-per-byte agree more with vision models on 1,024 image–caption pairs. The cross-modal score "only reaches 0.16" of 1, is maximised over layer pairs, and the metric was chosen after CKA "revealed a very weak trend". It is local neighbourhood agreement that rises with competence, not kernel equality and not convergence to a model of reality. | Active |
| [THEORY-683](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-683.md) | Permuting a fixed set of few-shot examples moves a GPT-family model's classification accuracy between near chance and near the supervised state of the art, at every model size tested; the good orders are specific to the model, the spread survives more examples and calibration, and bad orders mostly fail by predicting one label | Lu et al. (2021, ACL 2022), [LIT-833](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-833.md), read in [NOTE-626](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-626.md). All 24 orders of four balanced SST-2 examples give accuracies from about 50% to above 85%, in GPT-2 and GPT-3 models of eight sizes; Spearman correlations of order accuracy between sizes lie between −0.35 and 0.27 (175B against 2.7B: 0.05). The variance stays high up to 32 examples and after calibration. It is a measurement on causal GPT models and text classification, with the transfer analysis resting on one example set, and the paper finds no property of an order that predicts its effect. | Active |
| [THEORY-698](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-698.md) | Thresholding linear attribute probes on a language model's embeddings yields a complete concept lattice for any incidence whatever, so the lattice is guaranteed by construction; what the Lattice Representation Hypothesis measured is per-attribute agreement with GPT-4o annotations at F1 70–83, and no lattice law | Xiong (2026), [LIT-267](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-267.md), read in [NOTE-240](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-240.md). Theorem 1 is the basic theorem of formal concept analysis applied to the crisp relation got by thresholding Fisher-LDA probes, and it holds for every binary relation; the paper's own proof plan says so. The empirical content is that the thresholded probes on three 7–8B models agree with a GPT-4o-annotated incidence at macro F1 69.7–83.2 and predict WordNet subsumption at F1 57.1–77.1. No closure, absorption or recovered-lattice comparison is tested, and the paper's join is not a lattice join as written. It is not evidence that language models encode a lattice beyond the incidence. | Active |
| [THEORY-719](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-719.md) | On a finite augmentation space, over unconstrained functions of the two views, the spectral contrastive and NT-Logistic losses are both minimized at the positive-pair density ratio | Johnson, El Hanchi & Maddison (2023), [LIT-258](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-258.md), App. B.2–B.3, read in [NOTE-751](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-751.md): on a finite augmentation space, with every function of the two views allowed, the spectral contrastive loss is minimized by K⁺ = p⁺/(p⊗p) exactly, and the NT-Logistic loss with equal positive and negative classes by the log-odds log K⁺, so its exponentiated score is K⁺. Population optima over unconstrained functions only; not what an encoder reaches, and not InfoNCE, which is [THEORY-001](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-001.md)'s open part. | Active |
| [THEORY-723](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-723.md) | For the final embedding and unembedding of a softmax model, the output distribution fixes the representations only up to an invertible linear map, and whether closeness in distribution bounds representational dissimilarity depends on the distance: not for KL in the saturation regime, but yes for the log-likelihood variance distance | Nielsen et al. (2025), [LIT-253](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-253.md), read in full in [NOTE-738](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-738.md), with Harvey, Larsen & Williams (2023), [LIT-250](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-250.md), for the kernel side. What is observed fixes a representation only up to that observation's symmetry group: a centred linear kernel up to a translation and an orthogonal map ([THEORY-004](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-004.md)), and a softmax output distribution up to an invertible linear map of the embedding with the inverse transpose on the unembedding (Thm 2.2). KL can go to zero while the embeddings stay non-linearly related (Thm 3.1, Cor. 3.2), but d_LLV ≤ ε gives d_f,g ≤ 2Mε (Thm 4.7). Final layer only. It does not say what the Platonic hypothesis means; that is [THEORY-002](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-002.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-728](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-728.md) | On a finite data set, a symmetric positive affinity normalized to a Markov operator is conjugate to a symmetric one, and its eigenvectors scaled by powers of their eigenvalues embed the data so that Euclidean distance equals the diffusion distance weighted by the inverse stationary law | Coifman et al. (2005), [LIT-981](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-981.md), skimmed in [NOTE-784](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-784.md), with the derivation written out here because the paper's equations were not seen. For n points and a symmetric affinity K with positive entries, A = D⁻¹K is a Markov matrix with stationary law π ∝ d. It is conjugate to the symmetric D^(-1/2) K D^(-1/2), so its eigenvalues are real and in [−1, 1], and in [0, 1] when K is positive semi-definite. The map x ↦ (λ_j^m ψ_j(x))_{j≥1} turns the m-step diffusion distance, weighted by 1/π, into Euclidean distance exactly. Truncation gives a lower bound. It says nothing about the continuum limit, which is [THEORY-565](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-565.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-730](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-730.md) | For an embedding whose Gram matrix is the absolute co-occurrence deviation matrix at full rank, words on a periodic lattice whose positive and negative co-occurrence parts each depend only on separation have Fourier modes of the lattice as principal components, in degenerate cos/sin pairs with amplitude the square root of the kernel's Fourier transform, and the exponential kernel gives a closed loop with integer frequencies on a periodic lattice and an open curve with non-integer frequencies on an interval | Karkada, Korchinski, Nava, Wyart & Bahri (2026), [LIT-860](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-860.md), Propositions 1, 3 and 4 and Corollary 2, with the proofs in Appendix E followed in [NOTE-664](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-664.md). The result is conditional throughout. It concerns an idealised embedding with W Wᵀ = \|M*\| and d ≥ rank M*, not a trained one. It needs the positive and negative parts of M* to be translation invariant separately (Assumption B.1), not M* alone. It says nothing about whether any corpus or model satisfies these conditions, which is [THEORY-183](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-183.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-732](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-732.md) | For ReLU networks interpolated linearly between two endpoints, weak additivity and commutativity at every layer make each layer's features exactly the interpolation of the endpoints' features, output-layer linearity bounds the path's error by twice the endpoints', and for one hidden layer with interpolating minima linear mode connectivity alone gives the exact case | Zhou et al. (2023), [LIT-674](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-674.md), read in [NOTE-512](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-512.md) with Appendix A's proofs checked: for an L-layer ReLU MLP on a finite dataset, weak additivity of ReLU over the two networks' pre-activations and the commutativity W_A H_B + W_B H_A = W_A H_A + W_B H_B at every layer make the interpolated network's features at every layer exactly the interpolation of the endpoints' features (Theorem 1). Output-layer linearity, at any positive scale, keeps the path's error within twice the endpoints' (Lemma 1). Lubana et al. (2022), [LIT-669](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-669.md), Lemma 2: for one hidden layer and interpolating minima, linear mode connectivity forces shared activation patterns, and with shared patterns the hidden features are linear along the path. It says nothing about when the conditions hold. That trained pairs satisfy them is [THEORY-111](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-111.md)'s empirical claim. | Active |
| [THEORY-734](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-734.md) | In the hyperbolic plane, a root carrying deg_max ≥ 15 chains of length m, embedded with worst-case distortion 1 + ε for ε ≤ 1, forces some node to hyperbolic distance at least (ℓ/(4ε))·ln(deg_max/(π√2)) from the origin, so fixed-point Poincaré coordinates need Ω((ℓ/ε) log deg_max) bits | Sala, De Sa, Gu and Ré (2018), [LIT-874](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-874.md), Lemma D.1, read in [NOTE-679](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-679.md), with the proof redone here without the paper's small-angle approximation. Only the root's children are used to fix the embedding's scale c, and then the chains turn the scale into depth. Plane only, one family of trees, fixed-point coordinates in the Poincaré disk, deg_max ≥ 15 and ε ≤ 1. It says nothing about H^r for r > 2, or about whether any tree needs fewer bits under another number system. | Active |
| [THEORY-737](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-737.md) | In a spectral contrastive graph that joins labelled known classes to unlabelled data, the least-squares residual of a novel labelling on the top-k eigenspace, with the labelled entries left free, equals exactly the part of the labelling outside that eigenspace that the labelled rows of the discarded eigenvectors cannot absorb | Sun, Shi, Liang & Li (2023), [LIT-235](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-235.md), Theorem 5.5 with its proof in C.1, read in [NOTE-833](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-833.md). The paper states the identity as ≤, and its proof is a chain of equalities. Re-derived here in three steps from orthogonality and least squares. With the paper's Lemma 5.1 it bounds the novel labelling's 0–1 linear-probe error by twice this residual. It is about the exact rank-k factorization of a population graph, not about trained networks. | Active |
| [THEORY-738](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-738.md) | In the unconstrained-features max-margin problem with k classes under step imbalance and feature dimension at least k − 1, the unique optimal logits are the simplex-encoded labels, every margin equals one, and the classifier and embedding Gram matrices are the two square-root factors of that matrix's singular value decomposition; the geometry is the simplex equiangular tight frame exactly when the classes are balanced or there are two of them | Thrampoulidis, Kini, Vakilian and Behnia (2022), [LIT-994](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-994.md), Theorem 1 and Corollary 1.3, read in [NOTE-764](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-764.md) and re-derived here. By [THEORY-726](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-726.md) the problem is nuclear-norm minimisation of the logits under margin constraints. The polar factor of the simplex-encoded label matrix certifies it optimal, because under step imbalance its off-diagonal entries are negative. It does not say that gradient descent or trained networks reach this geometry, which is [THEORY-286](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-286.md)'s. | Active |
| [THEORY-739](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-739.md) | For the quartic proxy of word2vec with tied weights, symmetric reweighting and constant weights, the rank-d minimisers are the top d eigenvectors of the relative deviation-from-independence matrix M*, scaled by the square roots of their eigenvalues, up to rotation; and from an initialisation aligned with those eigenvectors, gradient flow acquires each one in an independent logistic rise, in order of eigenvalue | Karkada, Simon, Bahri and DeWeese (2025), [LIT-855](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-855.md), Theorem 1 and Proposition 2, read in [NOTE-660](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-660.md) and re-derived here. The quartic proxy is a function of WWᵀ alone, so von Neumann's trace inequality gives its rank-d minimisers. Gradient flow from an aligned start keeps the eigenbasis and reduces each mode to a logistic equation. It does not say that word2vec, or the proxy from random initialisation, behaves this way; that is [THEORY-182](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-182.md)'s. | Active |
| [THEORY-740](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-740.md) | A two-layer linear network trained by gradient flow on white inputs from a decoupled, balanced start learns each singular mode of its input–output correlation in a logistic rise that waits a time of order its inverse strength times the log of the inverse initial scale, so the modes arrive one at a time in order of strength; a single-layer network on the same data learns every mode on one timescale with no plateau, so under these conditions the stages come from the product of layers and the data's spectrum | Saxe, McClelland and Ganguli (2014, 2019), [LIT-864](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-864.md) and [LIT-862](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-862.md), read in [NOTE-667](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-667.md) and [NOTE-666](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-666.md), re-derived here. From a decoupled, balanced start the two-layer equations keep the SVD basis of Σyx, and each mode's strength obeys τȧ = 2a(s − a), a logistic rise. One weight matrix on the same data relaxes every mode exponentially on the one timescale τ. It does not say that random starts follow the solution, which is [THEORY-186](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-186.md)'s. | Active |
| [THEORY-745](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-745.md) | For the reversible walk p = k/d built from a symmetric non-negative kernel on a finite connected set, the t-step diffusion distance is exactly the Euclidean distance between the coordinates λ_l^t ψ_l, and keeping only the coordinates with \|λ_l\|^t > δ\|λ₁\|^t errs in D_t² by at most δ²\|λ₁\|^{2t}(1/π(x) + 1/π(y)), an absolute bound and not the relative accuracy δ that Coifman and Lafon state; the truncated maps are nested as t grows, so with δ fixed the steps t order a refinement chain by eigenvalue modulus, while untruncated they are all invertible images of one another | Coifman and Lafon (2006), [LIT-1246](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1246.md), read in full in [NOTE-985](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-985.md).
